summary.en: Past forms usually mark gender and number rather than person.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 2 and 3.

Russian past-tense verbs do not change for first, second or third person. Instead, they reflect the gender and number of the subject:

| Subject | Past of быть | Everyday verb |
|---|---|---|
| masculine singular | был | оставил |
| feminine singular | была | пришла |
| neuter singular | было | подъехало |
| plural | были | нашли |

Because **я** and **ты** take the gender of the real person, Matvey tells Kira **ты пришла на десять минут раньше** (*you arrived ten minutes early*, feminine **пришла**), while neuter **такси** takes **такси подъехало** (*the taxi pulled up*), and plural **отели** takes **все отели были полные** (*all the hotels were full*).

Watch out for impersonal absence with **не было** (*there was no*): in **масла в холодильнике совсем не было** (*there was no butter in the fridge at all*), **было** stays neuter singular while **масла** is genitive.

On replay, connect each past ending directly to who or what performed the action—including the speaker's own gender when the subject is **я** or **ты**.
